title: Agent Council
markdown:
The Executive (`openexecutive.orchestrator.executive.Executive`) is a single coherent persona that fans out to specialist sub-agents via Anthropic tool use. Each specialist subclasses `openexecutive.agents.base.BaseAgent`, carrying a `name`, `domain`, and `model`, and exposes `analyze(...)`, which wraps the question in user-turn context and calls Claude through the per-call provider.

Routing uses one `consult_specialist` tool. Multiple parallel `tool_use` blocks in a single assistant turn fan out concurrently through `router.route_parallel`, each running its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query before the specialist sees the question. The Executive then synthesizes the returned analyses into one reply.

The ten entries in `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY` (`openexecutive.orchestrator.router`):

| Key | Agent | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cso` | `StrategyAgent` | strategy |
| `cfo` | `FinanceAgent` | finance |
| `chro` | `HRAgent` | hr |
| `gc` | `LegalAgent` | legal |
| `coo` | `OperationsAgent` | operations |
| `cmo` | `MarketingAgent` | marketing |
| `cpo` | `ProductAgent` | product |
| `board_comms` | `BoardCommsAgent` | board |
| `talent` | `TalentAgent` | talent |
| `triage` | `TriageAgent` | triage |

Models: specialists default to `claude-sonnet-5`; a deep-reasoning tier uses `claude-opus-5` (adaptive thinking); routing/fast classification uses `claude-haiku-4-5`. The Council's **Deep reasoning** toggle is honoured on Claude Opus/Sonnet (direct or via OpenRouter) and on any OpenRouter model whose live catalog entry supports `reasoning` (today all OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and Grok entries; not Llama) — the request translator turns Anthropic adaptive thinking + effort into OpenRouter's `reasoning` parameter. It is a silent no-op on models that can't reason, and disabled for Haiku, which rejects adaptive thinking. With `OPENROUTER_ENABLED`, the Council dropdown's non-Anthropic entries come from OpenRouter's live `/models` catalog (fetched at startup, refreshed in the background, filtered to tool-capable paid text models from an allowlisted vendor set), falling back to a built-in snapshot if the fetch fails. Four Council-only agents (`quality_judge`, `utility_fast`, `research`, `fixture_generator`) are model/prompt-overridable in the UI but not callable via `consult_specialist`.

Most specialists only *advise* — they return analysis the Executive synthesizes. The `talent` specialist (Head of Talent & Executive Search) additionally backs a vertical the Executive can *act* on: `orchestrator.talent_tools` gives the main tool loop read access to the live search pipeline (`list_engagements`, `list_candidates`, `get_candidate`, `match_candidates`) plus two side-effecting tools (`set_candidate_stage`, `start_talent_workflow`), so a chat turn can move a candidate or fire a screen/outreach workflow, not just opine. See the Talent section.

Beyond the talent vertical, the Executive can launch *any* workflow conversationally: `orchestrator.workflow_run_tools` adds `list_workflows` (the launchable catalog with each workflow's inputs) and `run_workflow` (runs a built-in or custom workflow to completion and returns its artifact, checkpointing approval gates as `awaiting_human`). This makes the `/jobs` catalog reachable from chat — see the Workflows section.

The Executive also backs the **Ask OE** panel's form-fill tier via `orchestrator.form_tools.propose_form_values`: when a chat turn arrives with a `<page_context>` block describing a form on the user's screen, the Executive can propose values for it. The proposal is delivered to the UI as a `form_patch` SSE event and placed into the form as highlighted suggestions — the tool never saves or submits anything; the user reviews and saves manually. The tool is **always** in the tool list (tool definitions sit at the top of the cached prompt prefix, so a conditionally-present tool would invalidate the prompt cache whenever panel and non-panel turns alternate); its description restricts usage to turns that carry a form descriptor.
